newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON ADMITS 4-0 WIN "BEYOND MY DREAMS".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON ADMITS 4-0 WIN "BEYOND MY DREAMS".

text.p: Manchester United coach Alex Ferguson admitted his team's superb 4-0 European Cup quarter-final victory over Porto on Wednesday was "beyond my dreams".

United, evoking memories of the 1950s and 1960s when they regularly crushed opponents at Old Trafford on European nights, are now virtually certain of a place in the semifinals of the European Cup for the first time since 1969.

They bamboozled Porto, who had won all their three away matches in the Champions' League phase of the competition, with goals from David May (22nd), Eric Cantona (34th), Ryan Giggs (61st) and Andy Cole (80th).
At the other end, apart from a scare in the opening minute, they did not allow Porto one serious goal attempt.
United, unbeaten in their last 16 English league matches, displayed a sense of control, maturity and professionalism missing in some of their previous European encounters over the past few years.

But with Giggs and Cantona outstanding and the entire team following their tactical plan to the letter, United look as though they could be a match for any other team in the competition -- with the probable exception of holders Juventus.
The Italian side beat them home and away in the league phase and could yet meet them again in the final in Munich in May.

Ferguson said: "I think that was one of the greatest performances by a United side in my 10 years here. They played with a really positive attitude and maturity and I can't praise them enough. They were marvellous.
"Before the match I would have been happy if we had won 1-0 and kept a clean sheet. The fact we have won 4-0 is beyond my dreams."
In contrast, Porto coach Antonio Oliveira refused to answer questions about his team's performance.
"I am too disappointed," he said, adding briefly: "I congratulate Manchester United. It will be very hard for us to advance now but I hope you see more of the real Porto in two weeks."
United's win came despite the absence of their combative Irish midfielder Roy Keane, who failed to recover from an ankle injury.
Ferguson said afterwards he decided to play with Cole and Ole Solskjaer in an attacking formation. It was a plan that paid off hansomely.
The first goal came when David Beckham's long cross was headed on by Gary Pallister. Goalkeeper Hilario failed to hold the ball and May swept it home from close range.

Cantona made it 2-0 when he took advantage of a mistake by Aloisio to lash the ball under Hilario's body from 12 metres. Giggs completed the 21-year-old goalkeeper's personal nightmare when he failed to stop a shot from the Welsh winger squeezing past him on his near post.

Cantona was the provider for Cole to score United's fourth 10 minutes from time to serve up a repeat of the scoreline when Porto lost at Old Trafford in 1977. They had won the first leg of that Cup Winners' Cup tie 5-2 at home.
But a repeat of that scoreline is highly unlikely on Wednesday's evidence, especially as Porto will be without key players Artur, Rui Barros and Sergio Conceicao.
They will be suspended after picking up second yellow cards on Wednesday.
